Chapter 12: Healing, Forgiveness, and Moving Forward.
The work of antiracism—let’s be honest—it’s tough. It brings up pain. Old wounds, new hurts, memories of injustice... all of it comes to the surface. Healing isn’t always easy, and forgiveness? Sometimes, it just feels out of reach. But without some kind of healing, we simply can’t keep going.
Imagine a community reeling after something devastating—a racist attack, a hateful message, maybe even a betrayal of trust. The anger is raw. The grief goes deep. Some folks want to move on as fast as possible, hoping to just forget and forgive. But others? They need time. Time to process. To mourn. To call for accountability.
Here’s something a lot of people miss: healing is needed everywhere, not just for those directly harmed. Racism doesn’t just leave a mark on individuals. It wounds families, entire communities. The divisions it creates? They can linger for generations.
For those who stick with the work, it becomes clear—healing isn’t a single moment. It’s a process. It takes honesty. It means really acknowledging the harm that’s been done, and being willing to listen, even when it’s uncomfortable. Healing happens when we create spaces for people to share their stories. Where pain isn’t brushed aside, and hope can begin to grow again.
Forgiveness? That’s a personal choice. It’s never something you can force, and it shouldn’t be rushed. But when it does happen—when someone is ready—it can open doors you might not expect. It creates room for growth, for new connections, for a future that isn’t chained to the past.
So, the work of antiracism isn’t just about fighting against injustice. It’s about building something better. A world where healing is possible for everyone. Where every single person truly feels like they belong.
